questions.ask: What exactly does a termination-point terminate or represent? Please give a gloss, example, and relations to TE nodes and TE links.
Is a supporting-TP itself a point, a relationship between client/server termination points, or an adaptation link? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
What does a tunnel-termination-point denote, and is it a service-access point, a tunnel endpoint, or both? Please give an example and relations.
Does a TE tunnel denote an externally requested end-to-end connectivity service or an internal traffic-engineered realization? Please give a gloss, example, and endpoint relations.
Does an OTN label encode multiplex/layer structure such as ODU2 mapped into OTU4, or does it identify an allocated switching resource? Please give an example and relations.
Does the connectivity matrix express constraints on permitted cross-connects among ports within one node? Please give an example and relations.
What is a tunnel-connection-endpoint, especially how it differs from a tunnel-termination-point? Please give an example and relations to tunnels and nodes.

proposals.rationale: Both appear to denote a forwarding/topological node in the modeled traffic-engineering domain.
Both denote a topological/traffic-engineering link between nodes, with termination points at its ends.
Both denote the topology container holding the domain's modeled nodes and links.

experiments.question: Does provisioning this pair preserve the adaptation object’s identity and client/server layer relationship, rather than confusing an adaptation link with a supporting endpoint?
Does a service-interface point translate to a tunnel-termination point while preserving external access identity and endpoint relationships?

answers.gloss: A termination point on a TE node at which a TE link terminates; it represents the node-local endpoint of that link.
answers.example: tp-R1-R2 is the termination point on R1 for the R1-R2 TE link.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and terminates i.telink. A TE link is terminated by termination points at its endpoint nodes.

answers.gloss: The supporting relationship by which a client-layer termination point is supported by a server-layer termination point. It is modeled as an adaptation concept rather than merely another ordinary TP.
answers.example: An OTN termination point at R1 supported by an optical-layer termination point at R1.
answers.relations: It connects client/server-layer termination semantics and supports i.tp. The decisive experiment confirmed identity with t.translink.

answers.gloss: The node-local trail head at which a TE tunnel originates or terminates. It is a tunnel endpoint, not inherently an externally exposed service-access point.
answers.example: ttp-A1 is the originating head of the A1-A3 ODU2 tunnel on node A1.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and originates or terminates i.tunnel. The decisive experiment refuted correspondence with t.sip.

answers.gloss: An end-to-end traffic-engineered realization carrying a service across a TE topology. It is the engineered tunnel itself, rather than a generic externally requested connectivity-service abstraction.
answers.example: The A1-A3 ODU2 tunnel engineered over the OTN layer network.
answers.relations: It originates and terminates at i.ttp, runs over i.tetopo, has internal i.tcep endpoints, and can be labeled by i.otnlabel.

answers.gloss: An OTN forwarding/multiplexing label expressing tributary-port and tributary-slot structure for a carried ODU signal.
answers.example: The TS/TPN values selecting the tributary slots that carry an ODU2 within an OTU4.
answers.relations: It labels i.tunnel. It encodes multiplex structure and can identify the selected slot resources; it is not merely the name of a layer protocol.

answers.gloss: A node-local matrix specifying which internal connections or cross-connects are permitted among termination points within a node.
answers.example: R2's matrix allows an incoming OTN termination point to connect to selected outgoing OTN termination points while prohibiting other combinations.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and constrains the node's permissible internal switching connectivity.

answers.gloss: An endpoint of a tunnel connection within a node. It identifies where the tunnel's connection realization enters, leaves, or is represented internally at that node.
answers.example: tcep-a1a3-R1 is the connection endpoint for the A1-A3 tunnel on R1.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and part of i.tunnel. Unlike i.ttp, which is the end-to-end tunnel's originating or terminating trail head, i.tcep represents an endpoint of the tunnel connection realization within a node.

questions.ask: Since the experiment refuted t.sip <-> i.ttp, what precisely is a service-interface-point: an externally exposed service access point, a client-facing boundary, or something else? Please give an example and relations.
Does connectivity-service denote an external service request/intent, the realized connection or tunnel, or both? Please give endpoints, example, and relations.
What information does layer-protocol-qualifier carry? Does it select concrete OTN tributary slots/TPN resources, or only qualify the protocol/layer type? Please give an example and relations.
Does a node-rule-group enumerate permitted internal cross-connects, group ports subject to common rules, or express another switching constraint? Please give an example and relations.
What does connection-end-point denote, and is it an endpoint of an internal connection realization, an end-to-end service, or a node-local connection? Please distinguish it from t.ltp and t.sip.

proposals.rationale: Both denote a node-local termination point at which a topological link terminates.

ratifications.reason: Both denote a node participating in the modeled per-layer traffic-engineering topology.
Both denote an inter-node topological/TE link terminated at node-local termination points.
Both denote the topology or per-layer network containing the modeled nodes and links.

answers.gloss: An externally exposed, client-facing service access point where a client requests or consumes network connectivity; it is not the node-local head of an engineered tunnel.
answers.example: sip-A1-odu is the ODU2 client hand-off at access node A1 for the A1–A3 service.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and provides access to t.cs. It differs from t.ltp, which terminates a topological link, and from a tunnel endpoint such as i.ttp. The decisive experiment refuted t.sip <-> i.ttp.

answers.gloss: An end-to-end connectivity-service abstraction representing the externally meaningful service, rather than merely its internal engineered tunnel realization.
answers.example: cs-a1a3-odu2 is the requested ODU2 connectivity service from A1 to A3.
answers.relations: It uses t.sip access points, is realized by t.cep connection endpoints, runs over t.topo, and is qualified by t.lpq. A tunnel may potentially realize it, but service intent and tunnel realization are not assumed identical.

answers.gloss: A qualifier describing the protocol, multiplexing, and client/server layer structure of a signal.
answers.example: The qualification that an ODU2 client signal is mapped into an OTU4 server signal.
answers.relations: It qualifies t.cs and is referenced by the layer adaptation represented by t.translink. It describes multiplex/layer structure; the model does not define it as a concrete allocation of tributary-slot or TPN resources.

answers.gloss: A node-local rule group specifying constraints on which ports or edge points may be internally cross-connected.
answers.example: The R2 cross-connect rule group permits selected incoming-to-outgoing OTN port combinations and prohibits others.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and constrains permissible internal switching connectivity among that node's ports.

answers.gloss: A node-local endpoint of the connection realization associated with an end-to-end connectivity service.
answers.example: cep-a1a3-R1 is the connection endpoint for the A1–A3 service on R1.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and part of t.cs. Unlike t.ltp, it does not terminate a topological link; unlike t.sip, it is an internal connection-realization endpoint rather than the external client-facing service boundary.

proposals.rationale: Both specify node-local constraints on permitted internal cross-connects among termination points or ports.
Both denote a node-local endpoint of the internal connection realization associated with an end-to-end service or tunnel.

ratifications.reason: Both denote a node-owned edge or termination point at which an inter-node topological link terminates.

experiments.question: Does translating the external connectivity-service abstraction as the engineered TE tunnel preserve endpoint identity, especially SIP-based service access versus TTP-based tunnel heads, and preserve the distinction between requested service and internal realization?

Does translating a protocol/layer multiplex qualifier as an OTN forwarding label preserve identity and capacity semantics, or does it incorrectly turn an abstract ODU2-in-OTU4 qualification into a concrete tributary-slot/TPN allocation?

proposals.rationale: The decisive experiment confirmed identity: both represent the client/server-layer adaptation relationship linking supported and supporting termination semantics.
The decisive experiment confirmed that these preserve the same end-to-end connectivity identity and endpoint relationships despite differing service-versus-realization terminology.
The decisive experiment confirmed that their multiplex and layer-qualification semantics correspond, including preservation of relevant capacity structure.

ratifications.reason: Both denote node-local switching constraints specifying which internal cross-connects among ports or termination points are permitted.
Both denote a node-local endpoint of the connection realization associated with the end-to-end tunnel or connectivity service, distinct from topological link termination and external service access.
Accepted; the decisive experiment confirmed identity, preserving the client/server layer adaptation relationship.
Accepted; the decisive experiment confirmed equivalent end-to-end connectivity identity and endpoint relationships despite differing terminology.
Accepted; the decisive experiment confirmed correspondence of multiplex/layer qualification and relevant capacity structure.
